report.summary: Chunk 2 of 4: defines _coverage_db, Mutant dataclass, trivially_equivalent, _code_fingerprint, _fn_source, _mutate_tree. Claims partially checkable.
risks: _coverage_db | medium | Function returns empty dict on all errors, silently ignoring all coverage databases. | Add logging or raise on failure to distinguish 'no coverage' from 'error'.

trivially_equivalent | medium | Claim 'safe on arbitrary repository source' may be false if compile() triggers import hooks or side effects. | Verify compile() does not execute imports or cause side effects on arbitrary source.
_code_fingerprint | low | Excluding co_flags bit 0x20 (CO_NOFREE) may omit important flag differences; justification unclear. | Document why CO_NOFREE is excluded.
_fn_source | low | Returns empty string as second element, which seems unused. | Confirm second element is intentional or remove.
_mutate_tree | medium | Only processes first function in AST; ignores classes, lambdas, module-level code. | Document limitation or add handling for other constructs.
todos: Add logging to _coverage_db when coverage database exists but fails to read.
Document safe compilation assumptions in trivially_equivalent.
Clarify the purpose of _fn_source's second return value.
Extend _mutate_tree to handle multiple functions and other callable forms.

handoff.purpose: Define coverage loading, Mutant dataclass, equivalence check, fingerprint, source slicing, and mutation tree transformation.

symbols.name: _coverage_db
symbols.note: Reads .coverage SQLite databases; returns coverage dict or {} on failure.

symbols.name: Mutant
symbols.note: Dataclass for generated defects; compatible with hand-written Mutation.

symbols.name: trivially_equivalent
symbols.note: Compares bytecode fingerprints of two source strings.

symbols.name: _code_fingerprint
symbols.note: Recursive structural fingerprint of code objects.

claims.text: caller must treat ``{}`` as 'unknown', never as 'nothing is covered'.
claims.why: Function returns {} on all failure paths and when no database exists.

claims.text: Field-compatible with the hand-written corpus's ``Mutation`` where it matters (``id``, ``defect_class``, ``file``), so the same measurement code reads both.
claims.why: No definition of Mutation provided in this chunk.

claims.text: True if the two sources compile to IDENTICAL bytecode.
claims.why: Function calls compile() and compares fingerprints; fingerprints include co_code.

claims.text: A mutant that compiles to the same code object cannot change behaviour, so it is undetectable by ANY method.
claims.why: Claim about behaviour equivalence is logical but not verifiable from code alone.

claims.text: Counting such mutants in a denominator silently lowers every score for a reason that has nothing to do with the detector.
claims.why: Not testable from this chunk; depends on external scoring logic.

claims.text: The literature puts the equivalent-mutant rate at roughly 10-40% (Jia & Harman's 2011 survey, per a research pass on 2026-07-30 -- the attribution is SECOND-HAND and unverified here; the filter below is not, because it is executed).
claims.why: Literature reference not verifiable from code.

claims.text: Bytecode identity catches only the trivial cases: a genuinely equivalent mutant with different bytecode still slips through, so this is a LOWER bound on equivalence and the residue stays unknown.
claims.why: Function only checks bytecode fingerprint; does not claim to catch all equivalences.

claims.text: Compilation is not execution: ``compile()`` builds a code object and runs nothing, so this is safe on arbitrary repository source.
claims.why: Safety claim depends on compile() having no side effects; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Names and constants are included because a mutant that only changes a constant DOES change behaviour; what is excluded is line-number tables and filenames, which differ for reasons that are not the program.
claims.why: Fingerprint includes co_consts (with repr), co_names, co_varnames, but not co_linetable or co_filename.

claims.text: Uses ``ast.unparse`` on the whole function, which normalises formatting. That is FINE for this purpose and worth stating: the measurement compares the mutant against its own unparsed original, never against the raw file, so normalisation cannot masquerade as a change.
claims.why: Claim about measurement logic not in this chunk.

observations.what: _coverage_db iterates over two hardcoded paths; returns {} if none exist or all fail.
Mutant dataclass has frozen=True; properties find and replace alias before and after.
trivially_equivalent catches SyntaxError and ValueError; returns False on any compile failure.
_code_fingerprint includes co_code, consts (recursively fingerprinted or repr'd), co_names, co_varnames, co_argcount, co_kwonlyargcount, and co_flags masked with ~0x20.
_fn_source returns a tuple (source, empty string) or None; second element is always empty string.
_mutate_tree only processes the first statement in the AST body; expects a FunctionDef or AsyncFunctionDef.
